laws: Each flow stage carries a stage label, delivered volume, positive flow setpoint, optional reported duration, and optional temperature record.
A cycle recipe is a finite ordered stage schedule and does not manufacture missing temperature observations.
description: Dimension-safe reusable representation of an AFPS flow stage and finite cycle recipe; absent source temperatures remain absent values.

laws: Total delivered volume is the finite sum of stage volumes.
Hydraulic duration is the finite sum of stage volume divided by a supplied positive flow rate.
Under an explicitly supplied constant-flow hypothesis, delivered volume equals flow rate multiplied by hydraulic duration.
empirical_inputs: positive actual flow rates when a hydraulic duration is evaluated
description: Deductive dimensional accounting for finite flow schedules, kept conditional on positive supplied flow data.

laws: The adapter only packages a supplied Physlib FluidState and supplied SmoothContinuityEquation certificate.
No pump-setpoint equality, reactor solution, residence-time distribution, porous transport, advection-diffusion, reaction-flow coupling, or reactor-performance conclusion follows from packaging.
description: Thin conditional boundary to the admitted Physlib continuity API, with no claim that an AFPS reactor satisfies the model.

laws: The detailed schedule records the six Table 2 stages at the reported 80 mL/min setpoint.
The approximately 7 s amide-bond observation and 40 s per-residue observation remain provenance-bearing reported values distinct from calculated quantities.
No temperature value is asserted when the selected sanitized records supply none.
description: Transparent source record for the published AFPS schedule and rounded observations, without elevating them to experimental axioms.

laws: The six detailed volumes sum exactly to 50.4 mL.
At 80 mL/min the pure hydraulic duration is exactly 37.8 s.
The grouped coupling segment is 9.6 mL and 7.2 s and agrees in volume with the detailed priming-plus-coupling entries.
The nominal 40 s observation exceeds the exact hydraulic sum by 2.2 s.
No theorem identifies 37.8 s with 40 s or assigns a physical cause to the 2.2 s difference.
description: Exact, deductive checks over the reported protocol, explicitly preserving the rounded-observation boundary.

laws: Every step-yield value lies in the closed interval [0,1].
Overall yield is the finite product of step-yield values.
A constant step yield repeated n times has overall yield y^n.
If every one of n steps is at least y and 0 ≤ y ≤ 1, overall yield is at least y^n.
description: General finite multiplicative step-yield model independent of the AFPS empirical schedule.

laws: The 40 s per-residue value is represented as a sourced nominal duration, not as the exact Table 2 hydraulic duration.
The timing record carries provenance and does not assert zero overhead.
description: Provenance-bearing reported timing datum kept separate from idealized scheduling assumptions.

laws: Nominal cycle time is residue count times the reported seconds per residue only under an explicit zero-overhead idealization.
For 30 residues at 40 s per residue, nominal cycle time is exactly 1200 s and exactly 20 min.
Setup, switching, maintenance, purification, and downtime are excluded assumptions rather than inferred absences.
description: Idealized timing calculation that makes every excluded overhead category explicit.

laws: Chain-equivalent throughput is computed only from explicit uptime, parallel-line count, and positive nominal chain duration.
No annual production claim is unconditional.
ChemistryLib process feed/product ratios retain their stoichiometric mass semantics and are not reinterpreted as SPPS cycles or recycle.
empirical_inputs: any separately supplied feed/product mass model
description: Explicit idealized throughput assumptions and a thin boundary to ChemistryLib process mass semantics; never repurposes recycle as SPPS cycling.

laws: The record preserves 0.2 mol/L amino-acid stock, 2.8 mL amino-acid delivery, 0.17 mol/L activator stock, 2.8 mL activator delivery, 200 mg resin, 0.45 mmol/g loading, reported 5.6 mmol reagent, and roughly 6 equivalents with provenance.
Raw reported claims remain data even when mutually inconsistent.
empirical_inputs: all concentration, volume, resin mass, loading, amount, and equivalent claims from Supplementary Figure 2
description: Dimension-safe transparent record of both the numerical inputs and the conflicting reported reagent amount.

laws: 0.2 mol/L times 2.8 mL is exactly 0.56 mmol amino acid.
0.17 mol/L times 2.8 mL is exactly 0.476 mmol activator.
200 mg times 0.45 mmol/g is exactly 0.09 mmol resin loading.
The corresponding exact ratios are 56/9 equivalents amino acid and 238/45 equivalents activator, supporting rounded displays 6.22 and 5.29.
The calculated 0.56 mmol is unequal to the separately reported 5.6 mmol.
No theorem attributes the inconsistency to a typographical error or silently changes either source claim.
empirical_inputs: the preserved Supplementary Figure 2 source record
description: Deductive dimensional arithmetic exposing, rather than repairing, the tenfold reagent-amount inconsistency.

laws: Volume, positive volumetric flow, duration, temperature, amount, concentration, mass, and resin-loading types are thin abbreviations or wrappers over existing ChemistryLib quantities and ChemicalDimension; they are not a parallel unit system.
Unit constructors and concentration-times-volume, mass-times-loading, volume-divided-by-flow, and flow-times-duration operations delegate to ChemistryLib quantity arithmetic.
The adapter introduces no empirical constants.
description: Narrow AFPS unit vocabulary implemented entirely through released ChemistryLib quantity and chemical-dimension APIs.
